MikroTik CGNAT Generator

Generate carrier-grade NAT for RouterOS (RFC 6598) with aggregated netmap blocks — one rule per block gives every subscriber a fixed public IP, or TCP/UDP port blocks for exact RFC 7422 tracing — plus the mapping log, an abuse lookup and edge filters.

Split view

Every address in the range is mapped (network, gateway and broadcast too — harmless). It must start on a boundary of the pool's block size.

–

    RouterOS script

    
  
    
  
    How it works: the subscriber range is cut into blocks the same size as each public block, and each block gets a netmap onto the public block. Netmap keeps an address's position, so the 6th address of a block always becomes the 6th public IP. With one rule per block that covers every protocol and the router picks ports; with port blocks each block gets a TCP and a UDP rule with its own port range — two rules, because to-ports needs a port-based protocol and protocol takes a single value. NAT only evaluates the first packet of a connection — existing connections keep their old mapping until they end (/ip firewall connection remove [find] applies new rules at once but drops every connection). The docs' filter chain=forward src-address=100.64.0.0/10 out-interface=WAN action=drop is left out on purpose: the forward filter runs before source NAT, so on the CGNAT router it would drop all subscriber traffic.
    

    


    
  
    Mapping & abuse lookup
    
  
    
  
    
  
    
  
    Keep the CSV, dated, with your records. With port blocks, any public IP and port belongs to exactly one subscriber while this mapping is in force — the reduced logging RFC 7422 describes; with one rule per block, a public IP narrows it to the subscribers that share it. A different pool, range or allocation means a different mapping, so archive the old file before changing it.
